title: My workflow for building a 3D sports manager game with AI: deterministic match sim, an online league on Supabase, and test bots that play hundreds of in-game hours before every release
author: TrainingJaguar2187
selftext:
I'm a solo dev from Belgium and I just released Circuit Ball Manager on Android: a management sim for a fictional car-soccer esports circuit. You sign players, set your lineup, scout free agents and fight through qualifiers, Masters, Majors and a World Championship.

How I used AI:

• Code: almost the whole game (a JavaScript web app wrapped for Android) and the online backend (database + server functions) were written together with Claude. I described what I wanted, tested it on my phone, and iterated.

• Match engine: the 3D matches run a deterministic simulation from a seed, so every viewer sees exactly the same match at the same minute. That's what makes live spectating work online.

• Testing: AI-written bot scripts play hundreds of in-game hours, offline and online, before every release to catch bugs and balance problems.

What's in it:

• Online divisions with fixed real-time match times and best-of-3/5/7 series

• Watch other managers' matches live, with a viewer count

• Offline career with a full year calendar of tournaments

• Scouting, transfers, academy, sponsors

What I learned: AI is incredibly fast, but you still have to test everything yourself. Asking for one change at a time worked much better than giant prompts.

Feedback is very welcome, especially on onboarding and balance.
